notes.title: MAN New Lion’s City & Free Bus Expansion coming October 7!
notes.content:
[h1]On [b]October 7[/b] the time has come![/h1]  
Three major highlights arrive on the very same day:
The brand-new [b]MAN New Lion’s City[/b] Bus DLC makes its debut, all owners of the [b]Depot + South Route DLC[/b] receive a free large-scale [b]bus map expansion[/b], and [b]City Transport Simulator: Bus + Tram[/b] finally launches on [b]PlayStation 5[/b] and [b]Xbox Series X/S[/b].  
A perfect trio for everyone who has been waiting to take virtual public transport to the next level.  

[h2]MAN New Lion’s City – the next generation on the road[/h2]  
The new Bus DLC brings the entire MAN New Lion’s City family straight into your fleet—in one especially comprehensive package for €19.99. Many of you asked not to pay separately for each variant, and we’ve taken that feedback to heart. Starting October 7 you can look forward to [b]six buses[/b] that offer maximum variety and impressive realism.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/78ae5ce66ba52ba23ee976ec63d9c36999ab8611.jpg[/img]

At the core are three base models: [b]12C[/b], [b]18C[/b], and the brand-new [b]19C[/b]. [list]
[*][p][b]MAN New Lion’s City 12C[/b] – 12 m solo bus with great maneuverability, available with [b]2 or 3 doors[/b][/p][/*]
[*][p][b]MAN New Lion’s City 18C[/b] – 18 m articulated bus for maximum capacity, selectable with [b]3 or 4 doors[/b][/p][/*]
[*][p][b]MAN New Lion’s City 19C[/b] – 18.7 m articulated bus, the longest of the family, available with [b]3 or 4 doors[/b][/p][/*][/list]

At almost 19 meters, the New Lion’s City 19C is the longest bus of the entire lineup and an impressive sight in city traffic. Each version comes with different door configurations so you can find the perfect vehicle for every route and demand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/16bc64fb19ab1a385bf1e62764b9742df2c1fb37.jpg[/img]

We worked hard to recreate the new generation of the Lion’s City range as precisely as possible. From the highly detailed 3D model and a cockpit packed with controls to an authentic start/stop system, every detail shows careful craftsmanship.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/7e5a3209db7de93b50356b2e6cdc2144af6fba4e.jpg[/img]

A special highlight is the RGB ambient lighting, which you can customize through the vehicle menu. For unmistakable sound, all engine, door, and interior noises were recorded directly from real buses. Every drive feels like you’re at the wheel of a true modern city bus—complete with realistic vehicle physics, precise steering, and the natural momentum when starting or braking.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/271e2511b96f59f74d9f86176a01cc206007ac36.jpg[/img]

Thanks to close cooperation with [b]MAN Truck & Bus[/b], [b]Dr. Richard[/b], and the [b]Verkehrsverbund Ost-Region (VOR)[/b], liveries, destination displays, and all technical details are officially licensed. For anyone who values authenticity, this is the most comprehensive bus package yet for City Transport Simulator.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/dc80eaec496e8041872b66e3270a941f76f092be.jpg[/img]

👉 Add the MAN New Lion’s City to your wishlist now:  
https://store.steampowered.com/app/3864840/City_Transport_Simulator__Bus_DLC_MAN_New_Lions_City/

[h2]Free bus map expansion for Depot + South Route[/h2]  
Alongside the new Bus DLC, all owners of the [b]Depot + South Route DLC[/b] will receive a free map update that significantly expands your network.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/58412a873bf70bbec97604ce48bb3352f5c3fa98.jpg[/img]

Eight new bus stops—five of them completely new—take you deep into a vibrant high-rise district where glass facades, busy sidewalks, and bustling streets create an entirely new atmosphere. At the new stations in the business district you’ll need tight scheduling and large vehicles to handle the heavy passenger flow.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/ee9cc75f7b516f5c1cadc3315446f3c3bf4c5a89.jpg[/img]

A special highlight is the new terminal stop at [b]Shuji-Nakamura Square[/b], a central hub in the Japanese quarter where bus and tram lines meet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/29c4f834f43c1b9e85be4c7f670c929d048d3f53.jpg[/img]

There’s also a new connection point in [b]Eglundsdorf[/b]: a through-station that leads on via [b]Jakob-De-Zoet Street[/b] to the depot, which now features several dedicated bus stops. You can start or end your day here—just like tram drivers already do.

At the depot’s northern exit, two more new stations await, linking you via Town Hall North directly to the central station. These additions open up brand-new routing options and give the entire city a fresh, urban feel.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/5898b672f51ca605ad1c2628d7f612a4508c07d6.jpg[/img]

[h2]City Transport Simulator on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S[/h2]  
It’s finally happening: [b]City Transport Simulator: Bus + Tram[/b] launches on [b]PlayStation 5[/b] and [b]Xbox Series X/S[/b] on October 7. With the console release we’re introducing a new, more unified package system tailored specifically for consoles. Nothing changes for PC players—you can keep using the structure you know and will receive all content updates on the same day.

For more details, check out the FAQ on our Discord server and social media channels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/fbef51f282d200dc9c5078947ed8335745024e6e.jpg[/img]

[h2]Free update for all platforms[/h2]  
To round off this big release, we’re also publishing a free update for all platforms on October 7. Along with the new content, it delivers a range of optimizations and bug fixes based on community feedback to make your experience even smoother.

notes.title: City Transport Simulator Bus + Tram - Update v1.2.2
notes.content:
[h1]CTS Update v1.2.2 is here![/h1]

With version 1.2.2, City Transport Simulator receives a major update that noticeably improves immersion: signals have finally been adjusted so you’ll experience fewer delays. In addition, the update gives you new customization options for the stop chime, lets you transfer renamed stations to Sandbox Mode, and fixes numerous bugs.

For more info, check out our new video here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X_9japvTkM0

[h1]CTS v1.2.2 Changelog[/h1]

[h2]New Features[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Stop Chime[/b] can now be selected in the customization menu.
[*] [b]Flexity[/b]: Added camera and mirror adjustment.
[*] New [b]Indicator Off[/b] key binding available for buses.
[*] [b]Renamed Stations[/b] in Career Mode can now be [b]transferred to Sandbox Mode[/b].
[/list]

[h2]Improvements & Optimizations[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Signals reworked[/b] to significantly reduce waiting times.
[*] [b]Main Station[/b]: Adjusted speed limits.
[*] [b]Passenger system improved[/b]:

[list]
[*] Spawn only at stops with [b]actual departures[/b].
[*] Now check timetables and are assigned to a matching [b]line[/b].
[*] Players can easily walk [b]through passengers[/b] without getting stuck.
[/list]
[/list]

[h2]Vehicles[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]MAN Lion’s City[/b]:
[list]
[*] Fixed [b]artifacts and shading errors[/b] on the rear window.
[*] Removed [b]graphic glitch[/b] on the front destination display.
[*] Passengers now [b]board correctly[/b] at the starting position.
[*] Black exterior areas are now [b]properly glazed[/b].
[/list]
[*] [b]ECAS system[/b]: Improved kneeling function—no longer gets stuck, especially on articulated and double-axle buses.
[*] [b]MAN Lion’s City A23[/b] (3-door): Fixed double seat occupancy.
[*] [b]MAN Lion’s City A26/A47[/b]: Added mirror material at door 2.
[*] [b]E1[/b]: Line number now displays correctly.
[*] [b]R2.2b[/b]: Corrected cloudy window panes.
[*] [b]StadtRegioTram[/b]: Fixed mirror clipping when adjusting.
[*] [b]GT6[/b]: No penalty for deadman’s switch.
[*] [b]GT8N[/b]: Added vehicle length in selection menu.
[*] [b]ULF[/b]: Door release now reliably disengages the brake.
[*] [b]GT6[/b]: Added headlight beams.
[*] Adjusted [b]pantograph heights[/b].
[/list]

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Switch rod[/b] functional again.
[*] [b]Collision detection with AI vehicles[/b] corrected.
[*] Fixed issue where [b]vehicles ran red lights[/b] at intersections.
[*] Added [b]missing overhead line[/b] at Jakob-De-Zuet-Straße.
[*] Correctly positioned [b]stop marker[/b] at Toriyama Allee.
[*] Fixed issue where [b]fewer passengers appeared over time[/b].
[*] [b]In-game hints[/b] no longer repeatedly appear/disappear.
[*] Fixed issue where [b]view angle couldn’t be changed[/b] after seat adjustment.
[*] Resolved issue where the [b]steering wheel became unresponsive[/b] if mouse mode was set to “throttle/brake only”.
[/list]

notes.title: City Transport Simulator - Roadmap July Update
notes.content:
[h1]Welcome to the new roadmap for City Transport Simulator![/h1]
Since the release of [b]City Transport Simulator: Bus[/b], a lot has happened and we have received tons of feedback from you. Today, we are excited to finally present the new roadmap for City Transport Simulator!
In the coming months, you can expect not only bug fixes and small features but also real content highlights, new vehicles, expansions, and a look into the future of CTS.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/db300cb0ad5857b82dd4ce4d8991b47566b3d84b.jpg[/img]

[h2]Looking back at the launch of CTS: Bus[/h2]
In June, we released City Transport Simulator: Bus on Steam, making our vision of an all-in-one simulation a reality — a game where bus and tram traffic go hand in hand on a lively, constantly evolving map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/a0d1a6712d3d9fb207026f627935b01f84304e5c.png[/img]

But the release was just the beginning: just like with CTS: Tram, we plan long-term support with new content, major features, and of course integrating your feedback, which we’ve received in large amounts through Discord, Steam, and social media over the past weeks. Thank you for that!

[h2]Next update: Mouse control, improvements & more[/h2]
The next update is already on the horizon with one of the most requested features from you:

[b]Mouse control for buses[/b]
Using the ALT key or directly via the control settings, you will soon be able to steer your bus intuitively with the mouse — no gamepad or wheel required.

[b]Physics improvements for trams[/b]
The Flexity Vienna will get better acceleration on inclines, and the Munich R2.2b will have more realistic sinusoidal movement and swaying adjustments.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/5c7639fcff01ca8b019e0251d93b39e6842c5c5c.jpg[/img]

And after that, there will be more [b]updates[/b]:

[list]
[*] [b]AI and signal improvements[/b]
We continuously work on optimizing traffic lights, AI vehicles, and overall traffic dynamics.
[*] [b]More life inside vehicles[/b]
New passenger voices will add even more acoustic variety, plus new announcement voices in several languages including English, French, Polish, and Hungarian.
[/list]

[h2]More vehicles in the works![/h2]
Of course, we are also expanding the vehicle roster for CTS with real classics and more compact bus variants.

[h3][b]GT6 (Tram Classic):[/b][/h3]
The legendary articulated tram GT6 brings retro flair to Tramau. With its charming look, distinctive driving style, and historic interior, this vehicle is made for all nostalgia fans!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/b64ae654481642212404c3f23d933777e88c2992.jpg[/img]

[h3][b]MAN Lion’s City A47 & A26[/b][/h3]
With the [b]A47[/b] and [b]A26[/b], we expand the fleet with two exciting 10- and 15-meter variants of the MAN Lion’s City.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/b8fe441e6a068315b003576fbc5a609028cdb02e.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/140629555b5f56d4f918c16bb03cca65a5ad21d3.png[/img]

Both models bring fresh energy to your fleet and enable new deployment options! More info on release timing and features will follow in one of the upcoming updates.

[h2]Looking ahead: Autumn highlights & console release[/h2]
Autumn will bring the next big phase of CTS with a special focus on the [b]console release for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S[/b]. The game is already very advanced technically, and we are working closely with Sony and Microsoft to complete the final steps for launch.

[h2]Free map expansion for all Depot DLC owners[/h2]
With the big autumn release comes a comprehensive [b]free map expansion for everyone who owns the “Depot + Southern Lines” DLC[/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/5f6f4cff1616f1e225f318f750bc420f0006eaf5.jpg[/img]

The new route takes you through a completely redesigned city district with [b]high-rise buildings and an urban metropolitan flair[/b]. In contrast to the previous districts in Tramau, here you will experience a completely different vibe: faster, denser, more hectic!

Additionally, the route is brought to life by [b]new AI passengers in business attire[/b] and a higher passenger density. People on their way to the office, appointments, or meetings. This gives the neighborhood a whole new atmosphere.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/84c9524dfbddb796e1898f93fefb06a9900320c5.jpg[/img]

[b]And do you remember the big construction site at the tram depot in the south of the map?[/b] That exact construction site will be transformed into a [b]new bus parking lot[/b] with this update! From now on, you’ll be able to [b]start or end your shifts as a bus driver in the south of the map as well[/b]. This not only brings more variety to your routes but also expands your daily itineraries and how you play the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/2d6e14d37317f33bd9722fd436f022bef7766444.jpg[/img]

The bus map expansion will be released [b]simultaneously with the console release in autumn 2025[/b] and is, as mentioned, free for all who already own the [b]Depot + Southern Lines DLC[/b]. If you don’t have the DLC yet, no problem: it remains available and offers a large tram depot, new stops, and a completely different route layout even without the expansion.

[h2]The MAN New Lion’s City 12C & 18C[/h2]

notes.title: CTS: Bus is here – Thank You for an Amazing Launch!
notes.content:
[h1]Thank You for an Amazing Launch![/h1]

We're absolutely thrilled about the successful release of [b]City Transport Simulator: Bus[/b] – our very first fully self-developed game.

This was a huge step for us, and it means a lot to see how positively you've received the game. Whether it's on Steam, Discord, or social media: [b]your feedback[/b] has not only been incredibly plentiful, but also [b]super helpful[/b] – and that's exactly why we want to give you a [b]quick behind-the-scenes look[/b] at what we’re working on and what you can expect in the [b]next updates[/b].

[h2]🔧 First Update: Save Files Fixed[/h2]
Some of you experienced issues with your [b]previous save files[/b] at launch – especially Early Access players whose progress didn’t carry over correctly. This was due to changes in the save system we had to make when taking over publishing responsibilities, which caused a specific set of data to break.

With [b]today’s hotfix[/b], this issue is resolved. The game will now [b]automatically recognize your correct save data[/b] – no manual action required.

[h2]🛠 What’s Next? Our Immediate Goals[/h2]
Of course, we're already working on the next steps – your feedback has made it very clear which areas need improvement. A key point is that [b]AI-controlled bus lines[/b] are currently missing for CTS: Tram owners. We're aiming to fix this with the next update.

We've also been made aware of a [b]crash issue[/b] that can occur when using custom key bindings. A fix is already in the works. Until then, [b]resetting your key bindings in the control settings[/b] can help avoid crashes.

We’re also developing a [b]Field of View (FOV) setting[/b], so you can adjust the in-cabin view – especially useful if you need a better look at your mirrors, for example.

Another issue affects players who don’t own the Depot + South Line DLC: they're currently being [b]reset to Eglundsdorf station[/b] while driving trams. We’re already working on a solution for that as well.

[h2]🧠 AI & Traffic Light Behavior[/h2]
In parallel, we’re continuing to improve [b]traffic lights and right-of-way rules[/b], to make traffic flow more realistic and easier to understand. Optimization of signal cycles is ongoing, with the goal of speeding up traffic flow in a realistic way.

[h2]🎮 Bus Controls[/h2]
For those of you who prefer to play with a keyboard, we’ve included three different steering modes at launch:
[list]
[*] The [b]realistic mode[/b] adjusts the steering speed based on how fast you're driving.
[*] The [b]continuous mode[/b] features consistent recentering – in the future, it will also be fully customizable.
[*] And if you want full control, you can [b]turn off auto-centering completely[/b] – ideal for smooth, manual steering.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/5faeb0a5bbe79eae52bd4c52efc387b7d7f18457.jpg[/img]

You can also fine-tune [b]Force Feedback[/b] via the gameplay settings – just scroll down in the menu to adjust the values to your liking.

In upcoming updates, we’ll refine the [b]default settings for keyboard and controller users[/b] so that bus handling feels even more precise. We're also working on giving you more [b]customization options[/b] so you can truly tailor the driving experience to your style.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/09fe201d0f15f775c009da57ebbc5d5c25174f1e.jpg[/img]

[b]Mouse control[/b] is also in development, and will soon offer an intuitive new way to drive.

[h2]Tips for Wheel Setup Issues[/h2]
If you're currently having issues with your [b]steering wheel or pedals[/b], please double-check the [b]dead zones[/b] for all axes in the settings and adjust them as needed. If that doesn’t help, we recommend [b]calibrating each axis individually[/b] and trying again.

We're continuing to work on improvements here – and we also plan to include more presets for various wheel models in future updates.

[h2]🚌 3D Model Improvements[/h2]
We’ve been closely following your feedback on the [b]MAN Lion’s City[/b] – and it’s been very helpful.
In particular, your comments about [b]cockpit and passenger area details[/b] are guiding our current work. We're making targeted improvements to ensure the bus is even more accurate – visually and functionally.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/8a414ec66d962cf61485bd5e63e981729ab2f647.jpg[/img]

[h2]🚋 Tram Adjustments[/h2]
Of course, we haven’t forgotten about the [b]trams[/b]. Two key areas are currently our focus: fine-tuning the [b]acceleration of the Flexity Vienna[/b] to match reality more closely, and making the [b]typical swaying of the R2.2b[/b] feel even more authentic.

Our goal is to provide a truly realistic driving experience.

[h2]❤️ Thank You – and Stay Tuned![/h2]
The launch was just the beginning. For us, one thing is clear: this game thrives on its connection with you.

Your feedback directly shapes our daily work – whether it’s about bugs, suggestions, or new features. We're incredibly proud of what we’ve already accomplished with City Transport Simulator together with this community – and we can’t wait to see where it goes next.

Thank you for your support, and see you in the next update

We’re incredibly excited to finally announce [b]City Transport Simulator: Bus[/b]! After intense development, it’s ready: the ultimate, realistic, and fully immersive bus simulation experience is coming! 🎉

City Transport Simulator: Bus launches June 11 for PC on Steam, and in September for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.

You can watch the full event including interviews and announcements about Bus & Tram here: https://www.youtube.com/live/6UY2utuV1r8?feature=shared

[h2]What is City Transport Simulator: Bus?[/h2]

City Transport Simulator: Bus is not a DLC – it's a standalone game on the CTS platform, which also powers CTS: Tram. In CTS: Bus, you become a bus driver and build and manage your own transport company in a highly detailed, European-inspired city.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/65df2bb39de89e3343030fbe85d414834e6d7206.jpg[/img]

Take the wheel of real, officially licensed buses from MAN and Dr. Richard, all recreated down to the finest detail – including authentic logos and designs. Whether you prefer a classic solo bus or a longer articulated one, you'll find a wide variety of vehicles and ways to expand your fleet.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/ae0eb3b464928fef53cf43795038d323a51b4f37.jpg[/img]

[h2]How does the City Transport Simulator platform work?[/h2]

[b]City Transport Simulator[/b] is the technical foundation for [b]multiple standalone games[/b] – including CTS: Tram and CTS: Bus. [b]Each title can be played independently[/b]. You don’t need CTS: Tram to play CTS: Bus – and vice versa.

[b]CTS: Bus is not a DLC or add-on[/b] – it's a full-fledged standalone title with its own content, vehicles, and gameplay modes. You can start and play it entirely on its own.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/2a0c433e693f69a83db0f5f9340355875872423b.jpg[/img]

If you own both games, CTS will automatically recognize it and unlock all content seamlessly. No extra steps required – just launch CTS and enjoy everything you own.

The best part: even if you only own one of the games, the city will never feel empty. In [b]CTS: Tram, AI buses[/b] drive through the city – in [b]CTS: Bus, AI trams[/b] are part of the environment. This ensures a vibrant and believable city at all times. Only players who own both games can drive both vehicle types.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/b2af4687dd022e393649dadf908a50c1d24ece45.jpg[/img]

[h2]Feature Highlights:[/h2]

[list]
[*][b]Officially licensed buses:[/b] MAN Lions City A21 & A23, Gräf & Stift NL205 & NG235 – all authentically recreated with real-world details and liveries 🚍
[*][b]Massive route network with 80 stops:[/b] Create your own routes or use the sandbox mode with 8 pre-built lines 🚏
[*][b]Career & Sandbox modes:[/b] Experience varied gameplay – from managing your company to relaxing free rides 🎮
[*][b]Extensive customization:[/b] Choose from over 10 liveries and 50+ logos to personalize your fleet 🎨
[*][b]AI buses & tram traffic:[/b] Enjoy a lively city with AI-driven buses and trams independent of your own vehicles 🤖
[*][b]Steering wheel support:[/b] Play with your Logitech G29, Thrustmaster T300, HORI Truck Control System, or other popular wheels with built-in presets 🛞
[*][b]Shared platform with CTS: Tram:[/b] Play CTS: Bus and CTS: Tram separately or together – all content is included in a single installation and recognized automatically 📂
[*][b]Realistic city with high detail:[/b] The transport network and urban development are modeled after real European cities – perfect for sim fans 🏙️
[/list]

[h2]Release & What’s Next[/h2]

CTS: Bus will be available June 11 for PC on Steam!  
Console releases (PS5 and Xbox Series X|S) are planned for September. The delay is due to the complex console publishing transition – but we’re working hard to deliver the best experience there as well.

[h2]And what about CTS: Tram?[/h2]

Alongside the Bus release, we’re also rolling out a major update for CTS: Tram with many exciting additions:

[list]
[*][b]New stop styles[/b] from Berlin, Vienna, and Munich 🏙️
[*][b]Rename stops[/b] for more customization ✍️
[*][b]Choose your tracks[/b] freely for creative route design 🛤️
[*][b]AI buses[/b] in traffic for a more lively city 🚦
[*][b]Passengers react[/b] to your driving – with positive and negative effects 🎭
[*][b]AI cars honk[/b] if you break traffic rules – for realistic traffic vibes 🚗🔊
[*]And many [b]bug fixes, optimizations, and features[/b] to improve gameplay feel
[/list]

We guarantee: both Tram and Bus will continue to receive regular updates so both games evolve together and keep the city vibrant and alive.

[h2]What else is coming?[/h2]

We’re working on new vehicles like the iconic GT6 tram for summer and already developing the Tatra KT4D – stay tuned!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/ee1fe6f8532a32f823a4c72c4f8dce26bb4a8e0d.jpg[/img]

Also planned: Vienna as a fully new city map in 2026, with never-before-seen detailed routes for both Bus and Tram.

[b]🔹 Is City Transport Simulator: Tram being discontinued?[/b]
No! Quite the opposite. We’re committed to City Transport Simulator as an active, long-term project. It’s not being replaced, cancelled, or neglected!

ViewApp is now fully in charge of City Transport Simulator's development and publishing!

No – all previously purchased content and DLCs remain available and usable.

Yes! With the publishing now under ViewApp, we can tailor updates more directly to your needs and ensure a regular update schedule.

We want to act more independently in the long term, be closer to the community, and steer development more directly. This helps us react faster to your feedback and develop the game in the direction you want.

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram - Roadmap February Update
notes.content:
[h1]A Glimpse into the Future of City Transport Simulator[/h1]  

First of all, we would like to sincerely thank you for the great launch of [b]City Transport Simulator: Tram[/b]! Your support and constructive feedback mean the world to us. It shows that what we are building together has a strong and engaged player base behind it.

Of course, not everything went perfectly, and some issues have affected your gameplay experience. That's why today, we want to be transparent with you about what we're currently working on and what is planned for [b]City Transport Simulator[/b] in the near and distant future.

[h2]Stability and Bug Fixes[/h2]  

The first week was intense. We've been closely monitoring your feedback and are working hard on an update that will address the most reported issues. Right now, the focus is on crashes, especially those related to the [b]E1 tram model[/b] – both the player and AI versions.

[b]In the next patch, you can expect:[/b]  
- Fix for AI E1 trams getting stuck in traffic  
- Fix for crashes related to the E1  
- Fix for crashes on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S & PC  
- Corrections to the target and line display on the GT8N and E1  

Another important point is the [b]missing station announcements on consoles[/b]. Unfortunately, we still have to wait for an update to the plugin that handles these annotuncements, which will cause a slight delay. But rest assured, we will deliver the announcements as soon as we can. Since the crash fixes are a higher priority, we don’t want you to wait any longer for those.

[h2]AI Improvements, Feedback, and Dynamic Weather[/h2]  

The [b]optimization of the vehicle and passenger AI[/b] remains a central focus, particularly when it comes to realistic priority rules and smoother traffic flow. We also continue to pay attention to your feedback, which is why we are currently working on a [b]free track selection[/b] at certain termini when creating lines. The goal is to avoid traffic jams and make the simulation even more realistic together with improvements in tram AI.

Of course, [b]dynamic weather[/b] is still a major focus. Since we want to implement realistic effects such as changed driving behavior, functional windshield wipers, and heating, as well as adjusted passenger behavior, this feature will take a bit longer.

What is nearly finished, however, is the [b]fully customizable controls[/b]. We know that everyone has their own preferences when it comes to control settings, which is why you will soon be able to reassign all the relevant keys and functions for both keyboard and gamepad. Additional improvements for joystick configuration will also be coming.

[h2]What’s Next?[/h2]  

We want to give you more ways to personalize your gameplay experience in the future. Soon, you'll be able to not only [b]set custom names for stations[/b], but also give the city itself a name of your choice.

This is an important step in further enhancing immersion and turning your city into a personal, unique game world. We're also working on offering [b]station announcements in more languages[/b], making the experience even more authentic and international.

Additionally, we want to give you the ability to [b]customize the appearance of your stops[/b]. With different presets, inspired by [b]real cities[/b], your city's look will become more varied and lively.

[h2]Navigation and City Design[/h2]  

A major point of feedback was the [b]minimap[/b], which at times caused more confusion than help. Therefore, we are working on a new solution, similar to the green circles at the stations, that will guide you naturally through the city without being intrusive.

There will also be some changes to the map itself. In addition to further improvements to switches and signals, we plan to expand and decorate many of the inner-city streets to make the city even more immersive.

[h2]New Vehicles and Surprises[/h2]  

Yes, new vehicles are still planned! Which ones exactly will be kept a surprise for now, but we’re sure you won’t expect some of the models coming your way.

Thank you for your support and feedback. We look forward to continuing to work on [b]City Transport Simulator[/b] with you!

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram - Beta Update v0.4.0 now out!
notes.content:
[h1]Beta Update v0.4.0 – New Features, Improvements, and Bug Fixes[/h1]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wW0o-krU3_k

We are excited to announce the release of Beta Update 0.4.0 for City Transport Simulator: Tram! This update brings a number of exciting new features, important improvements, and bug fixes that enhance the overall gameplay experience. 

Attention: Please note that the beta update is optional and can currently lead to many crashes. It can also happen that the new storage system can cause the save data in the experimental update to be lost (but it will still be retained in the stable update!)

Here are the key changes:

[h2]New Features[/h2]
- Joystick support: You can now experience the game with joysticks and take full control!
- Two new map extensions: 6 new stations (including 2 terminal stations) with an old town atmosphere and grass tracks
- Controller preset: We’ve added predefined controller settings to get you started right away.
- Keyboard preset: New keyboard settings offer an improved control experience.
- Keychain collectible available: Collect the new item and expand your in-game collection!

[h2]Bug Fixes[/h2]
- Intersection at Stadtgraben: We’ve fixed an issue where cars at the intersection in Stadtgraben weren’t moving – everything is running smoothly now!
- Cockpit Legend achievement: The Cockpit Legend achievement now works as intended, so no more worries during your pursuit of achievements!
- Overall satisfaction: A general satisfaction of 5.0 is now possible again – meaning you can achieve even better results in the simulation!

[h2]Improvements[/h2]
- Upgrade to UE5.4: The game has been updated to the latest version of Unreal Engine 5.4, improving performance and stability.
- Hauptbahnhof through station: The Hauptbahnhof now features a through station – a perfect addition for your daily routes!
- Schmiedegasse advance signals: Advance signals are now present in Schmiedegasse, making the traffic situation even more realistic.

Beta Update 0.4.0 is now available for testing! We look forward to your feedback and continuing to improve the game. Have fun playing!

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram – Dev Diary Update #1
notes.content:
[h1]City Transport Simulator: Tram – Dev Diary Update #1[/h1]

Hello everyone,
We are excited to give you a deeper insight into the latest developments and improvements for City Transport Simulator: Tram. Due to the high demand from the community, we have decided to publish this Dev Diary to highlight some of the most important changes and bug fixes.

You can watch the video version of our Dev Diary here (only available in German): https://youtu.be/TrTk1GDnDEA

[h1]Overview: Recent Changes and Improvements[/h1]

In recent weeks, we have been working intensively to stabilize and optimize the gameplay experience in CTS: Tram. We are currently in an intensive testing phase of a new version of the game. We are working on testing and fixing the remaining bugs before we release the update.

[h2]New Gameplay Options[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/8e25555b3d73aaabb5ccc10b2b8613b3118ab7de.jpg[/img]

Some changes we've already implemented include new options that give players more control, such as:

[*] [b]Green Stop Markers:[/b] These can now be toggled on or off.
[*] [b]Tram Braking Power Adjustment:[/b] This option was added specifically for the "Type D" tram, which now has stronger braking power.
[*] [b]AI Density:[/b] The density of AI cars and pedestrians can now be set to "low," "medium," or "high." This improves the game’s adaptability to different performance configurations.

[h2]Improved AI Pedestrians and Vehicle Behavior[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/fcaa3bb49e45a13a1d60307d6cfe6e0a9ce49ad1.jpg[/img]

One of our focuses in the past weeks has been improving the behavior of AI vehicles and pedestrians. Here's an overview of the changes:

[*] [b]Traffic Lights and Pedestrians:[/b] Pedestrians now behave more realistically at traffic lights, no longer crossing on red, and respecting traffic rules.
[*] [b]AI Trams:[/b] AI trams now stop properly to allow passengers to board and disembark and no longer get stuck on the tracks.
[*] [b]Optimized Vehicle and Passenger Spawning:[/b] The spawn logic has been revised so that vehicles and passengers are now integrated more efficiently and realistically into the game without negatively impacting performance.

[h2]Gameplay Adjustments[/h2]

There are also gameplay improvements:

[*] [b]Green Markers:[/b] These now work as they should, accurately indicating when and where to make the perfect stop.
[*] [b]Distance Display:[/b] The HUD now accurately shows the distance to the next stop after being revised.
[*] [b]Collision Logic Adjusted:[/b] Collisions now occur more realistically and at the correct times—whether between trams, cars, or pedestrians.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/06347d73f2accb99dacdd9fab0be378bb72c21ac.jpg[/img]

[h2]Switches and Signals[/h2]

Another major update concerned the functioning of the switches and signals in the game.

All the signals you encounter in the game now work correctly and are respected by both your tram and AI vehicles. As a result, there are no longer any issues with trams running red lights or unexpectedly stopping.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/9689bc742ef0bc0ecde3d26f0bd131d24db2f8e9.jpg[/img]

Bugs related to switches have also been removed. The automatic switch recognition and control now work as intended, contributing to smoother gameplay.

[h1]Recap of Update 0.3.0 and What's Next[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/d3254d9211250f3b63a07dd0128c4b3dccb0ff8e.jpg[/img]

In the last update (version 0.3.0), we added many new features like the Type D tram, a map expansion, and over 100 new loading screens to enrich the game experience.

With the upcoming update 0.3.1, we will primarily focus on bug fixes and improvements. While there will be no new features, the update will deliver a more stable and immersive gameplay experience.

[h2]Console Versions[/h2]

Another major focus is the work on the console versions for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S. Particularly for the Xbox Series S, it’s been a challenge to achieve optimal performance without simply reducing graphics quality and AI density.

We are working on ensuring that the game runs on consoles at medium graphics settings with stable 60 FPS. These improvements will also benefit the PC version.

[h2]What’s Coming Next?[/h2]

In the coming weeks, our focus will be on thorough testing. We want to make sure all systems are working flawlessly before releasing the update. Since quality is our top priority, there is no exact release date for the update yet, but we are planning to roll it out within the next few weeks.

We are very pleased with the progress we've made and are looking forward to delivering Update 0.3.1 to you soon.

It’s important to us that the game runs smoothly and stably for all players—whether on PC or console. That’s why we are taking the time to test everything thoroughly.

Thank you for your patience and support! We’ll keep you updated and are eager to hear your feedback.

Stay tuned—there’s much more to come!

This huge update was supposed to address several of your requests, but unfortunately, errors crept in that should not have happened – and we take full responsibility for that.

[h2]What are we doing now?[/h2]
Our first priority is to revise our internal processes. As you may have noticed, we are taking more time than usual for the next update. The reason for this is that we want to make this update as stable as possible. We are focusing heavily on bug fixes and gameplay balancing to finally resolve issues like malfunctioning traffic lights, stations, switches, or AI trams. Additionally, we are improving our QA process and investing more time in testing to identify and fix errors earlier, before the update is released.

[h2]What does this mean for you?[/h2]
There will be delays with the next update. We will keep you regularly updated via our Steam page, social media channels and community Discord and inform you exactly about the progress and current status of the update.

[h2]What can you expect in the next update?[/h2]
We are focusing primarily on bug fixes and stability, so there won’t be any major new features. However, these improvements are coming:

[h3]AI Behavior[/h3]
- Passengers will no longer be stuck in the ground.
- AI trams will follow their correct routes and no longer stop unexpectedly.
- AI trams will no longer pass through player trams.
- Collisions with vehicles and pedestrians will be more realistic and won’t trigger too early.

[h3]Signals & Switches[/h3]
- All switches will function correctly and can be operated either automatically or manually.
- All (switch) signals will work correctly.
- Traffic light phases will be realistically and correctly timed.
- Warnings like "Signal Ignored" will only appear after actually passing the signal.

[h3]Stations[/h3]
- Green stop markers will always be displayed correctly and can be disabled in the settings.
- All stops will appear correctly on the map.
- The "Missed Stop" warning will only show up if the stop was actually missed.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3]
- Tram brake force can now be customized in the settings.
- Speed limits are displayed correctly.


At the same time, we are continuing to work on the [b]PS5 and Xbox Series X/S versions[/b] of CTS: Tram. We’ll be able to share more details on the console version in October and possibly even announce a release date.

We hope you understand that we are working hard on addressing these issues and doing our best to ensure that something like this doesn’t happen again in the future. City Transport Simulator is just as important to us as it is to you, and we are committed to delivering a high-quality and enjoyable simulation based on your feedback. Your player experience is our top priority, and we will continue to do everything we can to improve it continuously.

Thank you for your patience and support!

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram - Early Access Roadmap Update!
notes.content:
Welcome to the CTS: Tram Early Access Roadmap Update for July!

We have exciting news for you! Last week, we released a new update for City Transport Simulator: Tram. Early Access Version 0.1.3 includes several bug fixes based on your feedback from Discord and Steam. We have addressed issues with switches and graphic errors in R2.2b. Additionally, the ULF now operates as an AI tram in the city, and the stop announcements have been updated to "Next Stop" as requested by the community.

Unfortunately, the latest update also introduced a bug. If you start a session with the R2.2b in the evening or at night, the game might crash when the door opens. We are already working on a fix and will release it soon.

However, there’s a major update coming up that not only includes bug fixes but also introduces new features.

[h1]Version 0.2.0: New Features and Improvements[/h1]

We are excited to present all the details about City Transport Simulator: Tram Early Access Version 0.2.0! In addition to several bug fixes, this update will bring new features.

[h2]Quickplay Feature in Sandbox Mode[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/d7c3cdc5938c606a4aa04dff21d25698091c5394.png[/img]

You will finally be able to use the Quickplay feature in Sandbox Mode! This feature will generate a session with just one click, allowing you to start immediately. All lines, vehicles, and start times you’ve created in your Sandbox network will be randomly selected to quickly play any session.

[h2]Collectibles: Postcards[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/2c7f513022f677ec80618527e61039d74c0475e4.png[/img]

In Version 0.2.0, you will also receive the first collectible items: beautifully designed postcards that you can find throughout Tramau. You just need to locate the large postcard dispensers at specific landmarks to unlock a postcard. Each postcard will provide background stories about the landmarks, allowing you to dive deeper into Tramau.

[h2]First Map Expansion[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/d3e12cb1734ea8d20b36749b46b7060d696fdc5d.png[/img]

Version 0.2.0 will also introduce the first map expansion! Although initially planned for the second phase of Early Access, it’s ready earlier than expected. This update will add three new stations, including one end station. The southwestern part of the Tramau network will be expanded, creating new connections to the stations Amtsstraße, Friedlandstraße, and Igor-Yurkevic-Platz, providing more variety in your network.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/0529ec6440fd03d2d5a401adbee9028c3028c427.png[/img]

[h2]Updated Early Access Roadmap[/h2]

With this new update, we are also excited to show you the updated Early Access Roadmap. Based on your feedback and requests, we have added several new points. In addition to the map expansion coming in the next update, we will also introduce new liveries for all trams, which you can immediately use in Sandbox Mode and unlock progressively in Career Mode. We’ve come up with some really cool and also funny alternative liveries that we think you’ll love.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/b5603c4492e3a326823b21ea0e3d6ebcb7f225ed.jpg[/img]

[h2]Joystick Support and Further Updates[/h2]

In the first phase of our Early Access Roadmap, we have also added support for alternative controls for mouse & keyboard and controllers. Many of you have requested controls similar to TramSim and Train Sim World, which you will be able to select.

This is just the first phase of our control expansions. In the second phase, you will finally be able to use joysticks in City Transport Simulator: Tram. We are currently working on this functionality, which will take some time, so this feature is scheduled for the second phase of our Roadmap. Additionally, we plan to offer fully customizable key bindings. You will be able to assign any key on your keyboard or button on your controller to suit your preferred control setup.

[h2]Dovetail Direct Event[/h2]

We’ve already provided you with information about new updates and the updated Early Access Roadmap. But that’s not all! Our publisher Dovetail recently announced another Dovetail Direct Event on August 20th, and we will, of course, be participating with CTS: Tram. We will share some exciting new information about the development. Tune in to Dovetail on August 20th to find out what’s coming up in the next few months!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/fd8f8d34f3894e5989737329bdfa0e32d86ac674.jpg[/img]

[h3]Epic Game Store Release[/h3]

About a month ago, we released City Transport Simulator: Tram on Steam Early Access. We are now excited to announce that CTS: Tram will soon be available on the Epic Game Store in Early Access as well. We are currently finalizing the Epic Game Store version and hope to announce a release date soon. We are also continuing to work on the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S versions of City Transport Simulator: Tram. We don’t have new information on the release dates yet but will update you on our social media as soon as we know more. You can already wishlist CTS: Tram on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and the Epic Game Store to stay updated.

Join the discussion in our [Steam Forum](https://steamcommunity.com/app/2604480/discussions/), [Discord Server](https://discord.gg/viewapp-community-1053340211016372285), and explore our social media channels ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/@viewapp), [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/tramsimulation/), [TikTok](https://www.tiktok.com/@viewapp), [Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/tramsimulator)).

Sign up for the CTS: Tram Newsletter to get exclusive insights, behind-the-scenes content, and more – [click here](https://citytransportsimulator.com/) to join our mailing list!

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram - Early Access is Now Open!
notes.content:
Well, that was a quick month or so! With the wait now over, we’re delighted to announce that City Transport Simulator: Tram has finally entered into Early Access  on Steam! Be sure to watch our cool gameplay trailer that shows what’s in store for you as you travel around the city of Tramau.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2604480/City_Transport_Simulator_Tram/

The work doesn’t stop now that we’re in Early Access – check out our Roadmap  for all the exciting things we’ve got coming your way in the near and distant future. Big thanks to those who have already wishlisted City Transport Simulator: Tram, and to everyone who is planning on grabbing it while in the Early Access phase. 

[h2]About City Transport Simulator: Tram[/h2]

In City Transport Simulator: Tram, you will be playing the role of a tram driver, transporting passengers to their destinations around the city of Tramau.  Choose from three true-to-life real-world trams, each with its own cab, interior, mode, and function. Pick up and drop off passengers while adhering to the timetable as you become familiar with your favourite tram.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44790845/b6ac5fda517605fe5897ca584c269ea9830d2d9c.jpg[/img]

Brand new to City Transport Simulator: Tram is the introduction of a career mode! As Tramau’s new tram operations manager, it’s up to you to turn around the fortunes of the city’s tram network. Develop your tram operation into a city-spanning tram network by starting with limited resources and just one tram. As you progress and earn XP, you’ll increase the number of trams in your fleet, customise and edit your own timetables, and place over 100 possible tramlines wherever you like in order to link up 39 stations. 

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44790845/f2d745bc6e1c5b99b87837914ee85950608301a8.jpg[/img]

[h2]About Tramau[/h2]

While the trams in City Transport Simulator: Tram are true-to-life simulations of real-world trams, the city of Tramau is entirely of our own making. Tramau has a lot of awesome points of interest and architectural pieces reminiscent of Southern German cities for you to explore, as well as a rich and storied history going back to the 12th century. This was a crucial decision for us to make, because we didn't want the game to feel stifled if it were set in a city with a tram network already in place. This way, you can expand Tramau’s tram network and place stations wherever you like! There’s 22.5km worth of track at your disposal which will only increase as we continue to develop the game.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44790845/d4cf5e8fa71c697c53244e09277eac5772e3af36.jpg[/img]

[h2]About Early Access & Benefits[/h2]

Whether you’re a member of our passionate tram community or you’re new to the tram simulator experience, we love and welcome feedback. Going into Early Access means we can take all that feedback and apply it as we continue to improve the game and see it through to 1.0 release. We want City Transport Simulator: Tram to achieve its fullest potential, and we can only do that by going into Early Access and listening to what you have to say about it.

We’ve also got some pretty cool Early Access goodies for you all to enjoy! When you pick up the game in Early Access, you’ll get it at a reduced price than if you waited for full release! Early Access also includes some shiny new trams we’re still working on, and you’ll get those as soon as they’re ready; the ULF A1, and a modern Viennese tram.

[img]https://clan.akamai.steamstatic.com/images/44790845/469260da9d9405619defcac63ab2592a67e1caf7.jpg[/img]

If you want to keep up to date with latest news, development updates, and other fun things, be sure to follow us on our social channels ([url=https://discord.com/invite/viewapp-community-1053340211016372285]Discord[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/viewapp]Facebook[/url], [url=https://www.youtube.com/viewapp]YouTube[/url], [url=https://www.twitch.tv/viewapp]Twitch[/url], [url=https://www.instagram.com/tramsimulation?short_redirect=1]Instagram[/url], [url=https://www.tiktok.com/@viewapp]TikTok[/url], and [url=https://twitter.com/viewapp_gaming]Twitter/X[/url]), visit [url=www.citytransportsimulator.com]our official website[/url], and [url=https://live.dovetailgames.com/auth/register?hobby=trams]sign up to our mailing list[/url].

[h1]CTS: Tram - Early Access v0.1.1[/h1]

We are thrilled to announce that [b]City Transport Simulator: Tram[/b] is now officially out in Early Access!

In this Early Access phase, you can expect many new features, changes and bug fixes. Your feedback is invaluable to us as we continue to refine and enhance the game.

[h1]Known Issues[/h1]
As with any Early Access release, there are a few known issues that we are actively working on. Here is a list of current bugs and glitches:

[h3]Traffic:[/h3]
Parked cars can occasionally disappear or park with brake lights on.
AI trams might not activate their door release at stations.
AI trams might not stop at stations.
AI trams might show the wrong destination.
ULF A1/B1 AI tram is incorrectly displayed as StadtRegioTram.

[h3]Passenger Behavior:[/h3]
Passengers sometimes cross red lights at intersections.
Passengers may walk in circles at certain locations.
Passengers might appear standing in the ground at some stations.

[h3]Level Design:[/h3]
Tyre marks may flicker depending on graphics settings.
Some traffic light phases still require polishing and fixing.
"W" switch signals don't appear.
Green indicator circles may not appear at all stations.

[h3]Performance:[/h3]
There may be a slight performance drop right before a station announcement happens.

Thank you for your support and have fun playing!

notes.title: Pic of the Week #26 - Career Mode
notes.content:
City Transport Simulator: Tram will be released in less than a week in Early Access on Steam! Last week, we explored the sandbox mode and line creation. Today, we're diving into the career mode of CTS: Tram!

[h1]Week 26 - Career Mode[/h1]

In career mode, you step into the role of a newly qualified tram driver. Tramau, once one of the first cities with electric trams, has neglected its tram network in recent years. However, thanks to an investment from the mayor, the network is being revitalized, and new trams from across Europe are being introduced.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/f2d745bc6e1c5b99b87837914ee85950608301a8.jpg[/img]

You will start with the new Tramau Transit line network and get to drive the ULF from Vienna. You will also have the unique opportunity to help design the line network and take on increasing responsibility. Through your drives, you will collect experience points (XP), which allow the operation to acquire new trams and resources for larger lines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/91c1ab2d15a9ad30f547b3679955738dcc706aab.jpg[/img]

[h2]The Email System[/h2]

Throughout your career, you will receive regular emails from colleagues. These messages offer valuable tips, new tasks, and additional opportunities to advance your career. They help you master the challenges of the operation and give you insights during Early Access on how to optimize your service.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/5b00742e57eb812c674e9fff1c39ca2f4d8158b5.jpg[/img]

[h2]Earning XP and Leveling Up[/h2]

Follow the rules to earn XP and level up. You will be rewarded for adhering to speed limits, signaling correctly, respecting traffic lights, and stopping properly at stations. When you perform multiple correct actions in a row, you earn XP combos that accelerate your leveling process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/3c3ad70236d352d6a43ff5befe6590921b8af7cc.jpg[/img]

With enough XP, you unlock new levels, which reward you with resources for vehicles and lines, new logos for your operation, and additional trams that you can purchase in the market.

[h2]Passenger Satisfaction[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/f2f3432e942e1d94c1591b5f1d9f6cb70f6f7617.jpg[/img]

Your custom-created lines and schedules are evaluated based on passenger satisfaction in career mode. Make sure your lines are not only fun to drive but also offer tight intervals, good connections, and extensive network coverage. These factors affect the overall city satisfaction and give you XP bonuses, helping you level up faster and acquire better lines and vehicles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/82a626aa54cd8fbf0878a366ca9fcc9202d57ce1.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Pic of the Week #25 - Line Creation
notes.content:
Less than two weeks to go until City Transport Simulator: Tram finally launches in Early Access on Steam on June 20th. Today, we want to introduce you to the different game modes and the line creation feature.

[h1]Week 25 – Line Creation[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/18388f8f585ce0f6f3751c269bf06f95464e4cc7.png[/img]

A highlight in City Transport Simulator: Tram is the ability to create your own lines. This is made easy thanks to Tramau’s 22.5 km track network – our largest yet!

Simply choose a starting station, connect as many different stations as you like, and end the route at one of the ten terminus stations. You can also select the line color, the long and short name, and the code to enter into the IBIS, the onboard computer. Then, assign your trams to the line.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/db1af37e00a4c13485048b8e49816a7f422b436f.png[/img]

[h2]Passenger Management and Vehicle Deployment[/h2]

Each created line has a set number of passengers who will use it every hour. To transport these passengers, you will need appropriate vehicles. On the market, you can purchase various trams, differing in price, capacity, and passenger comfort.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/6e56ad2486c752672fdfe3c80a51da6eb257c883.png[/img]

Depending on the length and connectivity of a line, you may need more or fewer vehicles. It’s important to plan carefully and choose the right trams to ensure efficient passenger transport and maintain high satisfaction levels. The trams you select will actually operate on the assigned lines in Tramau!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/59d72c05b2a4590312be5d92c0e69bd218b0a9a7.png[/img]

[h2]Timetable and Interval Management[/h2]

In City Transport Simulator: Tram, you can not only create your own routes but also set the intervals and timetable. Simply set the start and end times for the line, then choose an interval between 3 minutes and 1 hour. The timetable will be automatically generated based on these settings.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/9d48150809e2a21cd54a3482b3375afaacc4aadf.png[/img]

The AI trams will follow the created routes and timetables. Be mindful of how you set intervals and times to avoid congestion and delays. Efficient timetables are just as important as connected lines to ensure smooth operations.

[h2]Career Mode and Sandbox Mode[/h2]

City Transport Simulator: Tram offers two different game modes: Career Mode and Sandbox Mode. In Career Mode, you can build your own operation by earning XP to unlock resources and vehicles. In Sandbox Mode, everything is already unlocked, allowing you to start driving all trams and create lines without any restrictions.

Sandbox Mode is perfect for players who want to create routes and schedules without limitations. Even if you don’t want to create your own lines, this mode includes six pre-made lines that work logically and cohesively. This means you can have a fully functional network from the first minute.

In today's Picture of the Week, we will delve into the extensive map of Tramau, which is a key feature of our game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/6647a3ce905bc6c14311df4f8e165420273373f5.jpg[/img]
Tramau's map is a massive and intricate network, offering over 100 different route possibilities for you to explore. The network spans approximately 22.5 kilometers and includes 39 stations, with 10 being terminus stations. This expansive and detailed map is designed to provide a diverse and challenging experience for all players.

The Tramau map takes you through various environments, from the bustling old town full of historical landmarks such as the St. Bernhards Cathedral, the Puls Center, and the City Hall, to quieter areas like the Eglundsdorf district. notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram - Early Access Roadmap
notes.content:
[h2]Hello and welcome to the very first CTS: Tram Roadmap! 
[/h2]
We are very excited to start sharing news about upcoming developments for CTS: Tram in these articles, and you can expect to see more of them down the line. 

This article and its future iterations will include updates on upcoming content, screenshots, trailers and behind-the-scenes news on current developments.

[i]Please note: The order of content shown in the Roadmap image gives a rough indication of the order we’ll be working on, but is subject to change. This does not take into account additional player feedback, which will be worked on alongside said content.[/i]

We’ll also be using data and feedback to best inform where we invest our development time.

This time, we want to highlight Early Access, which [b]will be available from June 20th[/b] on PC. We'll explain why we decided to go with Early Access and provide details about what you can expect during this period.

If you’re in a hurry, here’s a quick summary of what updates to expect next during the Early Access phase:

[h3]•	ULF A1
•	Quick Play
•	Postcards Collectible 
•	Junction Tutorial & Updated First Time Experience 
•	Updated Manuals
•	Updated Character Selection Screen & Titles
•	Ambient Sound improvements
•	AI traffic improvements [/h3]

[previewyoutube=YAFWOO3WeWI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h2]Why Early Access?[/h2]
We chose to go with Early Access, because we believe that, with your input, we can create the best gaming experience, as it provides us the opportunity to develop City Transport Simulator: Tram hand-in-hand with our community. 

This approach allows us to integrate real player feedback, ensuring that we create the most immersive and engaging tram simulation experience possible. Our team values player insights, and we believe this collaborative process will greatly enhance the game's quality and playability. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/dd9420f1bfd7444486b53ac3c3066ed67ff358a4.png[/img]

Our long-term vision for City Transport Simulator is over time to bring additional transport modes, expanding the maps and modes - these will be added via new paid-for releases, DLC and expansions. All of these will come after full launch, as separate releases. At the moment, however, our focus for CTS: Tram is to build the gameplay mechanics, city infrastructure, and immersion which we can use as a basis for building on in future. Our ultimate goal is to provide an entertaining, fun, varied, public transport simulator – with your feedback at the heart of it. 

[h1]What’s next?[/h1]
[h2]The Roadmap – First Stop[/h2]
 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/dd2393178472e567490866da188130eb24b54491.png[/img]

During Early Access we plan to introduce a slew of new features, separated into different phases, which we are lovingly calling “Stops”. Starting with the First Stop we’ll aim to introduce a new tram, collectibles, more gameplay features as well as finalise character selection, achievements and tutorials.

Then, in future updates, you can expect to see [b]map extensions[/b], [b]additional services[/b], [b]new trams[/b] and even more [b]gameplay features including dynamic weather and track events[/b] like malfunctions to make the experience even more immersive. All of this will be accompanied by updates and changes based on your feedback.

While all of this is still a work in progress and subject to change, let’s delve a bit deeper into what you can expect during the First Stop.

The highlight is certainly the addition of a new tram, namely the ULF A1, a further enhanced version of the ULF A. First introduced to Vienna in 2007 and with a much shorter length of 24,2 meters compared to the ULF B1, it is a perfect addition for your low-frequency timeslots.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/d5cf3493e9f73dd73cf9c8993a2e2a4cd977945d.png[/img]

We are also working on a narrative to further establish Tramau’s history and make it feel even more like a real city. If you haven’t done so yet, make sure to take a look at the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2604480]regular Pic Of The Week Updates[/url], as they provide a lot of insight into Tramau’s history and give you a look behind the curtain on how certain systems operate.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/8eb9cad8dd1b0354b4210b6f8306df55b8761d48.jpg[/img]

Want to learn more about the picturesque cathedral or the historical Tramau Central Station? Or are you more interested in how we implemented Passenger Information Systems, intersections or the highly detailed overhead lines? All of this and much more is waiting for you to be explored right now. 

The completionists among you will be able to look forward to collectables, hidden all over the city. These postcards will unlock more of Tramau’s history, adding even further to the authenticity of Tramau as a real, living and breathing city.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/f72833df3773089164c031c86940fe67ea1ac1d4.jpg[/img]

This first wave of updates will also introduce the Quick-Play function, allowing you to jump into the game right away. If you’re just hankering for a bit of tram driving, this mode is for you. 
Finally, the character selection and achievements will be finalized, and all tutorials will be introduced to the game.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/2578ed062e6bbc4a5f683f15960f5efb56143a83.png[/img]

[h2]Phase 2 and beyond[/h2]
After the conclusion of Phase 1, we move onto further updates. Much like the previous content, this is currently all a work in progress and subject to change, but for now let’s take a quick look at what is currently planned.

Tramau’s tram network offers a lot to explore from the get-go, but we would like to expand this even further and add more areas for you to delve into.  These expansions will add to the existing network seamlessly and allow you not only discover new areas in Tramau, but also give you more freedom to expand your network and interconnect it in new and exciting ways.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/6647a3ce905bc6c14311df4f8e165420273373f5.jpg[/img]

To keep things interesting, we are also working on a new, modern Viennese tram to be added in the future. We can’t reveal which one it is quite yet, but we hope you are excited and looking forward to another highly detailed and accurate vehicle to add to your collection.

Furthermore, we want to add to the immersive experience by adding AI trains at the main station and more varied passenger and AI car models.

You can also expect to hear more news about the dynamic weather feature, which introduces fog and rain effects which impact the driving behaviour of your tram. The dynamic passenger volume feature will make adjustments to how many passengers board your tram depending on the time of day, making nighttime drives calmer, but the midday rush all the more exciting.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/782f8ece76d6b4dcabe087b3d9ada3b8732314d6.png[/img]

And that is it for now! Make sure to [url=https://live.dovetailgames.com/live/city-transport-simulator/articles/article/city-transport-simulator-tram-coming-to-early-access]have a look at our announcement article[/url] as well, which will go into more detail about when and where to purchase City Transport Simulator: Tram.

notes.title: City Transport Simulator: Tram – Coming to Early Access!
notes.content:
Greetings tram drivers old and new, we’re so excited to announce that City Transport Simulator: Tram will be entering into Early Access on 20th June 2024.

You can still add City Transport Simulator: Tram to your Steam wishlist, and also be sure to sign up for our mailing list so you’ll be the first to know when we enter into Early Access.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/7cbaa80585af59ccab57117821a5f3d580a68930.jpg[/img] 

[h2]About City Transport Simulator: Tram[/h2]
Assume the role of a tram driver as you transport your passengers to their destinations all around the city of Tramau. Get set up in one of three true-to-life real-world trams, each with their own unique cabs, interiors, modes, and functions. Familiarise yourself with your favourite tram and start picking up and dropping off your passengers while sticking to the timetable.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/9a67b56e461f68f13131f3b064c9796eb4c7a92b.jpg[/img] 

The city’s tram network has seen better days, so it’s up to you to manage Tramau’s entire tram operation! Start with limited resources and a single tram as you gradually expand your small tram operation into a city-spanning customisable tram network. Add more trams to your fleet, customise and edit your own timetables, and position your own tramlines to link up your stations however you see fit!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/57d1953918ab98b0581de520e7c7b4bb4cfb8d91.jpg[/img] 

[h2]Welcome to Tramau[/h2]
Tramau is inspired by real-world cities found in southern Germany. We’ve worked hard to build Tramau to be as authentic as possible, producing a rich and storied history and unique points of interest, including a Baroque-style cathedral, a 14th century University, and a botanical garden constructed in the 18th century. We didn’t want you to be limited creatively by a real city when building out custom tramlines and stations, but rather, to truly make Tramau your own.

notes.title: Pic of the Week #22 - HUD Display
notes.content:
Welcome to the City Transport Simulator: Tram - Pic of the Week #22! This week, we focus on the HUD we have developed for CTS: Tram.

[h1]Week 22: HUD Display[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/ba43989d62621b0ffa1072d6b1e627c9a40ebc22.jpg[/img]

Our previous tram simulator, TramSim, didn’t have a HUD, which often led to players not knowing how fast they were going or what the speed limit was. Therefore, it was important to us from the beginning to integrate a HUD in CTS: Tram.

We created the first concept for the HUD back in July 2023. The goal was to unify all the information found in the tram into one place – the HUD. For this, we created a space at the bottom left that displayed speed, allowed speed, the next signal, the next two switches, the slope, and the amps. Additionally, there were IBIS information like the name and distance of the next stop, and the current punctuality.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/e0d7acdad191bf9d5d3bcd37dd27af19d41a3051.jpg[/img]

[h2]Initial Implementation and Overhaul[/h2]

Initially, the HUD was implemented into the game as designed. However, after several test phases, we noticed that it was too much information at once. Therefore, we simplified the HUD to include only the most important information. To complement this, we implemented a kind of minimap that shows the next switch positions and the location of the next stop. Additionally, we now show the route being driven with the selected color above the "Next Stop" and the distance to the next speed restriction below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/9904f7d4f6bf9a1ba940743ad3ae0b4c71858864.jpg[/img]

[h2]Career Mode and EXP Display[/h2]

On the right side of the HUD are all the important elements related to EXP in Career Mode. You earn a certain amount of EXP for correct driving (observing speed, signals, using indicators, etc.). This can also create a combo that awards even more EXP. At the top, you can see the current level, the total EXP, and the time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/8d3ad29401d653f3ddd036a84902ac1ecd5fde66.jpg[/img]

[h2]Objectives and Tips[/h2]

For tutorials and tips, there are specific "Objectives" in the top left. These help you quickly and easily understand what the next step is. Below these, you can also find notifications about the respective controls, such as whether the door release has been activated/deactivated or how much the lever has been moved.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/5004b9600ad96cd0b6649664ee07875b0d1519b6.jpg[/img]

Overall, we are very proud of the HUD display. It immensely helps to have all the important information at a glance, making tram driving even more beginner-friendly. Of course, it can also be turned off if you prefer the classic experience.

notes.title: Pic of the Week #21 - AI Traffic
notes.content:
Welcome to the Picture of the Week #21! Today, we delve into the world of AI traffic in City Transport Simulator: Tram.

[h1]Week 21: AI Traffic in Tramau[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/df43a3d5fbe3f16e77fa9e8698acce56812f7372.jpg[/img]

AI traffic is a crucial component that truly brings cities to life in a simulation. We've introduced some exciting improvements and innovations to enliven the streets of Tramau with realistic and intelligent traffic.

A vibrant city is characterized by a variety of vehicle types and colors on its streets. Therefore, we've integrated various types of cars in different colors to create a diverse traffic scene. From compact city cars to delivery vans – the streets of Tramau are bustling and diverse. Even a DHL delivery van can be found in the game!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/2145051732b535732ca9f92d9f9a22272ce0937c.jpg[/img]

[h2]Improved AI Technology[/h2]

The AI in the game has been completely overhauled and is now significantly smarter and more dynamic. This contributes to making the traffic in Tramau feel realistic and organic. Even parked cars have been faithfully recreated, including the correct angle of the wheels.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/c893d0373bcbec8adcdbb415b6fb70353f5d74b1.jpg[/img]

Another notable improvement is the adaptation of AI passengers. They now respond to the destination display of the tram and board or disembark accordingly. Additionally, they utilize all available seating in the tram regardless of the entry door and prefer seats over standing room. When they want to disembark, they move towards the door during the journey, rather than waiting until the tram has come to a stop.

[h2]Intelligent Traffic Light Control[/h2]

Controlling the traffic lights was a central focus in the development of Tramau. Since it's a fictional city, we had to redesign and implement the traffic light system from scratch. We aimed to make the traffic light sequence dynamic and realistic.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/5e6551cc67328c3d139264b20d126d73fde34f72.jpg[/img]

At tram stops, there are trigger points that switch the traffic lights to "stop" or "go" mode, similar to many real cities, to ensure the smooth flow of passengers.

[h2]Adaptation to Stop Areas[/h2]

In stop areas where there is a lane for cars between the tram and the stop, we're currently implementing special measures. Cars will stop before the tram stop to ensure the safety of passengers. This will allow passengers to reach and leave the trams without any risk, while other road users wait until boarding and alighting are complete.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/4d86cb1392d147de818fcc9cf6487fec49eddd9e.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Pic of the Week #20 - Intersections
notes.content:
Welcome to Pic of the Week #20! Today, we take a closer look at the intersections in City Transport Simulator: Tram and reveal the challenges and solutions we encountered during their implementation.

[h1]Week 20: Intersections[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/660302f9f30774186e0f10ddc1c29414f655c607.jpg[/img]

In Tramau, there are numerous intersections, and for good reason. Our goal with CTS: Tram is to provide a flexible network that offers many options for designing routes. Intersections allow for branching lines, creating a variety of different routes. However, integrating these intersections was no easy task and required extensive planning and adjustments.

[h2]Challenges of Switches[/h2]
One of the biggest challenges was accommodating the different requirements of various vehicle types. In particular, we needed to find a solution to allow trams, which can only choose between left and right, to turn in different directions. While the ULF and the StadtRegioTram have three direction options in the IBIS (left, right, straight), the R2.2b only has the option for left and right.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/cd5df3907ffb33d2cd13fcd335aadf3614cf9d66.jpg[/img]

To solve the intersection problem, we used two consecutive switches. The first switch allows the vehicle to go straight or turn right, while the second switch provides the option to go straight or turn left.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/c0efa6060263462a11b73e3503dc16c9c5f4dc5f.jpg[/img]

This configuration allows trams that want to go straight to choose left and then right. For a left turn, a tram selects the left direction twice, and for a right turn, it only needs to pass through one switch. These adjustments enable the R2.2b from Munich to now travel in three different directions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/9b897818fb5e5b46ee2404d1fff912d53a5c2d65.jpg[/img]

[h2]Improved Control[/h2]

Another significant enhancement was the implementation of key bindings for the switch controls, both on the keyboard and controller. This improvement will greatly facilitate the efficient use of the switch controls.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/45e69822bd019cf98b2940acbd07d5f9d4a890ba.jpg[/img]

notes.content:
Welcome to the nineteenth Pic of the Week! Today, we're taking a closer look at the city of Tramau and sharing how we've managed to craft it into an authentic German city.

[h1]Week 19: Crafting an Authentic City[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/c8923ba16e38f7b6d20379856534ac27efef0670.jpg[/img]

One of our key considerations was integrating well-known brands and stores that exist in the real world. In our previous games, we recreated real cities in photorealistic detail, benefiting from the panorama freedom laws. However, with Tramau being a fictional city, those laws no longer apply. Nevertheless, we were determined to include familiar German brands and stores.

[h2]Integration of Real Brands[/h2]

Securing licenses for these brands required significant organizational effort. Initially, we reached out to companies to explain the concept of CTS: Tram, which posed some challenges ("A fictional city, but with real brands?"). However, many companies quickly warmed up to the idea.

Subsequently, work began on creating 3D models and textures to incorporate these brands. It was crucial for us to maintain the authentic style of the brands and buildings. We requested reference material from the companies and conducted thorough online research. Some companies had specific guidelines for using their brand, which we respected.

[h2]The Result[/h2]

We've introduced Tegut as a grocery store and MediaMarkt and Saturn as electronic retailers, providing players with a diverse selection of familiar and varied shops.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/3a188c4c834740adfd31ed11380db71b3ed03233.jpg[/img]

Beyond integrating stores and logos, we've added props to bring the city to life. Thanks to our partnership with the Deutsche Post and DHL, we've included not just a parcel shop but also parcel stations and a DHL transporter in Tramau.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/bce46d5f2c6ec736f85b845954b4b81bbf5df5d1.jpg[/img]

notes.title: Pic of the Week #18 - Switches
notes.content:
Welcome to the 18th Pic of the Week! Today, we're diving into the world of switches and exploring their crucial role in City Transport Simulator: Tram.

[h1]Week 18: Switches[/h1]

Switches are an essential component of the tram network, allowing trams to travel in different directions as needed. They are indispensable for the flexibility and efficiency of public transportation, enabling trams to adjust their routes according to demand.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/da4c0c01c78202d01add360bc452a79381176fba.jpg[/img]

[h2]Structure and Operation[/h2]

A typical switch consists of several components, starting with a marker just before the switch, marked by a yellow triangle in Tramau. This marker signals to the switch that a tram is approaching. Once detected, the switch communicates with the IBIS system and automatically adjusts according to the planned route.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/ca8a782622ab5e60d11da5f9b1834d5c29b27a32.jpg[/img]

However, in CTS: Tram, it will be possible to deactivate the automatic switch setting in the settings. This will require manually adjusting all switches, similar to the process in Munich.

[h2]The Switch Signal[/h2]

The switch signal provides all the necessary information to safely cross the switch. Arrows at the top of the signal indicate the direction of the switch - left, right, or straight ahead. When a tram passes the yellow marker, an X symbol on the switch signal indicates that the switch can no longer be electrically adjusted.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/8eb9cad8dd1b0354b4210b6f8306df55b8761d48.jpg[/img]

If the X symbol is already displayed because a tram is passing over the switch, you must wait until the X symbol is no longer displayed before crossing the marker. This ensures that trams traveling in different directions (left, right, or straight ahead) can safely pass.

[h2]Manual or Automatic Control[/h2]

Automatic switch control is enabled by default in CTS: Tram but can be disabled in the settings. In this case, switches can be manually controlled via the IBIS system or by exiting the tram and manually adjusting them with a switch iron.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44790845/7db55c0b2d59204aa1f062ef3a6387cc8e7c0759.jpg[/img]
